Mars: Before & After ChemCam Laser strikes

Curiosity used its Chemistry Camera laser to acquire chemical composition data from three adjacent locations on a rock fragment that had been disturbed by the rovers wheels during an earlier drive. The surface of the rock had a coating of regolith (soil) which has been displaced by the resulting plasma from the series of laser strikes.

This collage consists of 2 remote micro images (RMI-ChemCam) that were acquired 'before & after' the laser strikes as well as a right mast camera image (R-MastCam) acquired after the strikes for context.

The target was located less than 2 meters north-east of the rover position on the morning of sol 1037 (July 7th, 2015). The local mean solar time (LMST) time stamps have been provided at the side of each of the images, these cover a period of around 50 minutes.

Has anyone here used an RSS feed? How do you use it? What do you use it for?

You subscribe to it with a reader application. You can get a standalone app for your OS or use something like feedly.com. Some browsers have an RSS reader built into them.

Any time the site that publishes the feed is updated they update their RSS feed and your reader app notifies you that the site was updated.

I use it for getting notification of updates to web comics and blogs mostly. Oh and podcasts.
I use it to sync podcasts to winamp. It's a lot less cumbersome than going to the website whenever I want to listen to one.

An RSS feed displays the latest posts from a particular site in a standardized structure that RSS Readers can convert into something much more readable for the user.

RSS feeds with RSS readers (ex: gReader on Android) allow you to subscribe to and organize of all the new posts from blogs, news sites, etc. On my phone I have a category for news, 1 for sports, 1 for gaming. Those categories contain the RSS feeds of all the sites I normally visit.

When viewing the posts in the RSS reader you typically get one of the images from the post and an abstract of the article (sometimes the full article). It allows you to bypass going to each individual site and view it all from one application.
